key_insight: Diffusion models are becoming the leading approach for medical image inpainting because they can generate anatomically plausible reconstructions across missing or corrupted regions.
clinical_relevance: These methods may support artifact removal, pseudo-healthy reconstruction, data augmentation, and anomaly detection in MRI and CT workflows.
method: Systematic review of 60 studies on diffusion-based medical image inpainting.
Taxonomy built around dominant architectures, including DDPMs and latent diffusion models.
Focus areas included artifact correction, augmentation, and downstream clinical tasks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a broad but uneven evidence base, with rapid growth in studies yet limited standardization in benchmarks, datasets, and validation across applications.
watch_item: Clinical translation is constrained by limited dataset diversity and inconsistent evaluation, so performance may not generalize well across imaging settings.
paper_title: Diffusion Models in Medical Image Inpainting: Challenges, Solution Taxonomy, and Future Directions
